subject.title: Feature Request: tools.cron.tools.deny config option for cron job tool restrictions

question: Should isolated cron jobs get first-class `tools.cron.tools.allow/deny`, inherit `tools.subagents.tools`, or continue with only per-job `payload.toolsAllow` plus delivery safeguards?
rationale: The answer defines a security-sensitive scheduled-run tool boundary and can alter existing message-delivery behavior for cron jobs.

options.title: Add Cron-Scoped Policy
options.body: Introduce `tools.cron.tools.allow/deny` with documented precedence and focused tests for message denial across cron delivery modes.

options.title: Inherit Subagent Policy
options.body: Apply `tools.subagents.tools` to cron sessions too, reducing config surface but coupling distinct execution modes.

options.title: Keep Per-Job Only
options.body: Avoid a new global cron policy and continue relying on `payload.toolsAllow`, docs, and delivery safeguards.

recommendation.title: Add Cron-Scoped Policy
recommendation.body: Introduce `tools.cron.tools.allow/deny` with documented precedence and focused tests for message denial across cron delivery modes.

likelyOwner.reason: steipete has both the prior review context for this exact issue and recent history in the policy/runtime area.
